newsitem.title: USA: Lott - US Senate bill to have more estate tax relief.
newsitem.headline: Lott - US Senate bill to have more estate tax relief.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Monday the Senate tax bill that will be unveiled this week will include more estate tax relief than legislation approved by the House Ways and Means Committee.
"We probably will have a little more on the estate tax than they do, so there will be some differences," Lott told reporters.

Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth, a Delaware Republican, is expected to unveil his tax bill Tuesday. The House Ways and Means Committee approved legislation last week for a net $85 billion tax cut over five years aimed at implementing the balanced budget agreement.
Lott said the Senate tax bill would have a "stronger" provision on the child tax credit than the House legislation.

"I think we will have a better package in the Senate Finance Committee on the ... tax credit for children," Lott said. "We will be a little stronger on the tax credit, particularly I think family groups will like those changes."
The House Ways and Means bill would gradually raise the threshold where the estate tax is imposed to $1 million in 2007 from $600,000 currently.

The estate tax provisions in the House bill would cost $28.6 billion over 10 years. An outline of proposals for the Senate Finance tax bill put the estimated cost of estate tax relief provisions at $32 billion over 10 years.
The bill approved by the House Ways and Means panel would provide a tax credit for children under age 17 of $400 in 1998 and then $500 after that.

The Senate Finance outline would allow a $500 per child tax credit for children under age 17 and parents with children age 13-16 would be required to deposit the $500 credit into an education Individual Retirement Account.
Asked about Roth's tax bill, Lott said: "I think it looks good, I thought (House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill) Archer's looked good too ... there's some minor differences between the two."
He added: "I think they're both very close to the mark of what we agreed to do."
